_readme: Plain words for Quick mode (assets/app.js). Terms: each gets a dotted underline the first time it appears on a page, and a tap shows its definition. Constitution: the plain name shown on a Constitution chip in Quick mode, by provision id from data/constitution.json (a clause without its own name uses its section's, then its article's or amendment's). One sentence each, neutral, no examples about real people. Anyone can suggest a change: edit this file.

terms.definition: A Senate vote to end debate on something so it can move to a final vote. It usually takes 60 of 100 senators.
Using long debate in the Senate to delay or block a vote. Ending one takes a cloture vote.
A vote to pass a bill even though the President or Governor vetoed it. In Congress it takes two-thirds of each chamber.
When the President or a Governor refuses to sign a bill that the legislature passed, so it does not become law unless the veto is overridden.
A small group of lawmakers that studies bills on one subject and decides which ones go to the full chamber for a vote.
A vote where each lawmaker's yes or no is recorded by name.
A question on the ballot that voters decide directly, instead of lawmakers.
The last vote a chamber takes on a bill. If it passes, the bill moves to the other chamber or to the President or Governor.
A proposed change to a bill, or a change added to the Constitution.
A formal statement by one or both chambers. Many resolutions do not become law.
A written order from the President or a Governor telling government agencies how to carry out the law.
The smallest number of members who must be present for a group to hold an official vote.
The person who holds the office now.
A group that collects money from members or donors and gives it to candidates or spends it on elections.
The money a campaign has in the bank on a given date.
A court decision issued in the name of the whole court, with no single judge named as the author.
A written opinion by a judge who disagrees with the court's decision.
A written opinion by a judge who agrees with the decision but gives different or extra reasons.
The Supreme Court's decision to take a case. Most requests are turned down.
A short summary at the top of a Supreme Court opinion, written by the Court's staff.
A person who lives in the area an official represents.
The group of elected lawmakers who write and pass a state's laws.
The two chambers that write federal laws: the House of Representatives and the Senate.
Someone the Federal Election Commission counts as a candidate because they registered and raised or spent more than $5,000.
